grade.rationale: The factory is generally well structured and produces deterministic projections, but several boundary-validation issues can produce internally inconsistent or incorrect reports. In particular, resolved findings are omitted from state counts, captured grade bands can disagree with normalized scores, and malformed or noncanonical metadata is not handled consistently.

summary: The implementation is readable and mostly decomposed into focused helpers. Correctness is weakened by inaccurate resolved-state reporting and insufficient normalization of snapshot-derived values. Error handling provides useful context for invalid root JSON but does not cover malformed nested metadata. Test coverage is unknown; focused tests should cover resolved findings, inconsistent grades, invalid enum values, and structurally malformed metadata.

grade.rationale: Summary counts and grade projections can be internally inconsistent, and noncanonical finding states or severities can silently disappear from aggregate results.
The code is divided into cohesive helpers and uses clear report-building stages, though ad hoc JSON traversal and repeated string-valued enums make invariants difficult to enforce.

Names and control flow are generally clear, but the distinction between all findings, current findings, and active findings is obscured by filtering resolved findings before constructing every state count.
Root JSON parsing errors receive useful path context, but type errors in nested metadata escape that boundary as low-level JSON exceptions.

Most behavior is implemented as deterministic transformations and is readily unit-testable, although extensive static coupling and untyped JSON access increase the number of edge cases required. Coverage is unknown.

findings.title: Resolved finding count is always zero
findings.description: The `current` collection removes every finding whose state is `resolved`, but `byState` is subsequently calculated exclusively from that filtered collection. Consequently, the emitted `resolved` entry is always zero even when observations contain resolved findings, making the report summary inaccurate.
findings.recommendation: Keep a deduplicated collection of all findings for `byState`, and derive the non-resolved and active collections separately. Define the duplicate-fingerprint precedence explicitly if observations can contain different states for the same fingerprint.

findings.title: Grade score and band can be inconsistent
findings.description: The numeric score is clamped to 0–100, while a captured `band` is accepted without validation and the fallback band is calculated from the original, unclamped value. Malformed or stale metadata can therefore produce a grade whose band does not correspond to its reported score.
findings.recommendation: Clamp the score once, derive the canonical band from that normalized score, and either ignore the captured band or validate that it matches before accepting the snapshot.

findings.title: Nested metadata shape errors bypass contextual error handling
findings.description: Only parsing and conversion of the root node are inside the contextual exception handler. Calls such as `AsArray`, `AsObject`, and `GetValue<T>` made afterward can throw for valid JSON with unexpected field types, exposing low-level exceptions without identifying the affected captured snapshot or path.
findings.recommendation: Deserialize into a typed DTO with validation, or include all metadata traversal in a narrow exception boundary that converts JSON shape/type failures into an `InvalidDataException` containing the observation path.

findings.title: Noncanonical finding states and severities silently corrupt aggregates
findings.description: Snapshot-derived severity and state strings are placed in the report without validating them against the supported values. Unknown severities, differently cased states, or other unexpected values remain on findings but are omitted from active, severity, and state counts, so detail records and summary totals can disagree.
findings.recommendation: Normalize both fields and validate them against the canonical severity and state sets. Reject invalid metadata with context or map it to an explicitly documented fallback before constructing the finding.
